title: Westbrook School Committee — School Committee Meeting

fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. The full committee (all seven members) and both student representatives were present. A brief 5:00 PM Finance Committee session immediately preceded this meeting (see the companion summary). For complete context, nuance, and anything not covered, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Chair Andrea Mancuso, Vice Chair Katy Rice, Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Noreen Poitras, Brooke Reed, Dr. Flynn Ross.

blocks.x: Dr. Lancia announced three retirements: Paula Curcio (Westbrook Middle School social studies teacher), Marina Davis (Westbrook High School math teacher), and Wendy Harvey (Westbrook High School co-principal, after 12 years as assistant and co-principal). He recognized extensive achievements. There were 35 Westbrook Regional Vocational Center students at the SkillsUSA state championships, with multiple medalists. The Westbrook Regional Vocational Center and Westbrook High School eSports team won two state championship titles. A Junior Achievement Titan Challenge state title unseated a longtime Yarmouth High School streak. Westbrook High School Winter Guard had a top-Maine, gold-New-England finish. There were also strong college acceptances, including Bowdoin, Colby, Boston University, and Northeastern. Details on the Pre-K admission lottery were to go out to interested families within a day or so. A student and a School Nutrition staff member were competing that day at the state cook-off after winning their regional round.
This is final approval of the calendar first approved March 11. It has no staggered Pre-K/kindergarten start, and students begin Monday, August 31.
Approved 7–0. Moved by Katy Rice, seconded by Erin Cavallaro.
New Business: FY27 Budget Public Hearing & First Reading
12.1 & 12.2 — Public Hearing on the Proposed FY27 Budget

The committee recessed into a public hearing on the proposed FY27 budget: $57,349,321.39, a 7.5% increase over FY26 (down from the original 9.88% March 4 proposal), a 7.34% increase to the local tax share. Mayor David Morse spoke during the earlier public-participation period. He thanked the committee and anticipated continued City Council support ahead of a June 9 voter referendum. No one spoke in person during the hearing itself. Three written comments were read into the record. One was in full support. Two urged the committee to keep instructional coach positions under consideration for elimination. One of those was from a Westbrook Middle School staff member about the middle school's two coaches. The other was from a Saccarappa teacher about the coaches' value there (partly read aloud, with the rest submitted in writing).
12.1 (recess into public hearing): approved 7–0. Moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Erin Cavallaro.
12.2 (close public hearing, return to session): approved 7–0. Moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Brooke Reed.

“From what I can piece together, the two instructional coach positions account for less than one-third of one percent of our proposed budget. The cost of keeping them is essentially a rounding error. The cost of losing them, however, would be felt by every teacher and by extension every student in the building...this is a cut we can't afford.”
blocks.cite: Pete Vernon, Westbrook Middle School staff member (written comment)

blocks.x: “What I observed in rooms with coaches present was collaboration with teachers through modeling and supporting...their guidance is always thoughtful, well-paced, innovative, and extremely helpful.”
blocks.cite: Jacqueline Dimmick, Saccarappa multilingual teacher (written comment)

blocks.x: 12.3 — Adoption of the FY27 Budget, First Reading (Roll Call Vote)

Finance Committee Chair Noreen Poitras read the full set of state-required budget warrant articles, which are separate budget questions approved by the Council and voters. They included the per-category breakdown: regular instruction ($21,712,387.01), special education ($10,633,908.71), career and technical education ($3,433,294.98), other instruction ($847,790.41), student and staff support ($4,600,998.09), system administration ($2,034,810.20), school administration ($2,430,076.55), transportation ($2,705,330.37), facility maintenance ($4,836,685.98), and debt service (yearly loan payments)/other commitments ($4,114,039.09). Chair Mancuso detailed roughly $1.3 million in total reductions from the original proposal (the increase falling from 9.88% to 7.5%). These included seven eliminated or reduced staff positions, $114,000 cut from technology, $60,000-plus from professional development, nearly $20,000 from athletics/activities, and roughly $70,000 from facilities. This vote was a first reading, the first of two required votes.
Approved 7–0 by roll call (first reading). Moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Allison Brunette.

“If we don't [hear from the community], we operate off of what's presented to us in a really thoughtful way, but it also...folks lose out on a chance to have a voice in a really transparent, public process. And I'll say that...I'm saddened that there was not more public input into our budget.”
blocks.cite: Erin Cavallaro, Board Member (on public engagement)

blocks.x: “Getting the deep dive look at this, I've been really appreciative of all the work that's done over several years to get to what is a really responsible budget.”
blocks.cite: Dr. Flynn Ross, Board Member (first budget cycle on the committee)

blocks.x: 12.4 — Waive Two School Days at Year-End

This is the annual routine request. It shifts the last day of school from Monday, June 22 to Wednesday, June 17 (both half days), since the calendar includes two more student days than the state minimum. It was taken as a combined first-and-final reading, meaning one vote that serves as both the first reading and the final, binding vote.
Approved unanimously, 7–0. Moved by Katy Rice, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
